desc:
AI image tagging and alt text for products gives every photo in your store a clear written description and useful tags. Ecom Swift LLC reviews your product images, writes short alt text and loads it into your store, or returns it as a sheet you can check first.

## What is alt text, and why does it matter for product photos?

Alt text is a short written description of an image. Screen readers speak it aloud for shoppers who cannot see the photo, and search engines read it to understand what the picture shows. If the field is empty, the image is invisible to both.

For a store, that means a blind shopper hears nothing about your best product, and Google Images gets almost no information about it. Many stores also leave filenames such as "IMG_4821.jpg" in place, which adds nothing. Good alt text and sensible tags fix both problems with a modest amount of careful writing.

## How image descriptions affect discovery and sales

Photos carry most of the buying decision in ecommerce, yet text decides whether the photo is found. A clear description helps your product appear in image search when someone types a phrase such as "green linen cushion cover". It also makes your store usable for customers who rely on assistive technology, which widens your audience and supports your accessibility duties.

Tags work inside your own store. When photos carry tags for color, style and setting, filters and related-product blocks can use them. A shopper looking at a lifestyle photo of a sofa in a bright living room can be shown other items tagged the same way. Results depend on your catalog and traffic, but accurate image data removes a common gap.

## What good image tagging includes

- Alt text that states what the picture shows, in plain language.
- Short descriptions, kept under 125 characters so screen readers handle them well.
- The product name and one or two real details, such as color or material, without keyword lists.
- A different description for each angle, so the back view is not described like the front.
- Decorative images marked so screen readers skip them.
- Tags for color, style, pattern and setting, such as studio shot or outdoor scene.
- A review list for photos that are unclear, cropped or hard to read.
- Suggested file names that describe the product instead of a camera number.
- A naming rule for future uploads, so the standard continues without us.
- A sheet of old and new values, so you can approve before anything changes.

## How we work

We begin with an export of your product images and their current alt text. We study each photo, often alongside the product title, so the description fits the item and does not guess at details the picture cannot show.

We write the text in a calm, factual voice. A photo of a ceramic mug becomes "White ceramic mug with a wooden handle on a kitchen counter", not a string of search terms. Where a picture is ambiguous, we add it to a review list instead of inventing an answer.

The Basic package delivers alt text for your main images as a sheet. The Standard package adds tags, marks decorative images and loads everything into your store. The Premium package covers a larger set, suggests better file names, uses the tags for on-site filtering, includes a hand check of a sample of images and leaves a naming rule for new uploads. Product feeds that use image data can benefit from the same tags.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Describe what is actually visible in the picture.
- Mention color, material or setting when it helps a shopper.
- Keep each description short and written as a normal sentence.
- Mark purely decorative images, such as dividers, as decorative.
- Use the same naming rule for every new photo you upload.

**Avoid:**
- Stuffing alt text with keywords or repeating the product name many times.
- Starting every description with "image of" or "picture of".
- Reusing one description across different angles.
- Describing details that are not in the photo.
- Leaving the field empty on product images, because a missing description is worse than a simple one.

## Who this is for

It suits a store whose photos were uploaded with default camera filenames and empty alt fields. It suits an owner preparing for an accessibility review who needs a fast first pass. It also suits a catalog owner who wants consistent image tags to power filters and collection pages.

## What we need from you

Send an export of your product images or a product export that includes image links, and tell us if some photos must be handled differently. We can work from links to your own store images, so you do not have to send files by email. We never ask for passwords: if you want us to load results directly, add us as a collaborator, staff or developer user with limited access.
